_comment: Generic evidence envelope for T1 item 8 (Characterization report),
DIGITAL partition. Issue #339. Shape and constraints: see the sibling
characterization-summary.analog.json's _comment and ./README.md -- not
repeated here.
WHY THE DIGITAL HALF IS CITED AT ALL, AND WHAT MADE IT DEFENSIBLE.
Item 8's text asks a digital (or mixed-signal digital) partition for
something the analog per-spec-row table does not carry: `Fmax, area, and
power across the corner set, not just functional pass/fail`. Those three
quantities exist, are committed, and are stable: the `klt
place-and-route` run under design/sar-logic/flow/sar_ctrl/reports/
measured area, and the post-route `klt sta` sweep measured Fmax and
estimated power at five corners against one fixed routed DEF. What did
NOT exist was an aggregation of them; issue #339 wrote the
`Digital partition (sar_ctrl_a)` section of
sim/characterization-summary.md, and this envelope asserts that section.
Citing the analog half only, and leaving 8.digital uncited, was the
alternative #339 considered and rejected: the evidence is not missing,
only unaggregated, and `no_evidence` would have been the wrong reason.
WHAT THIS `pass` MEANS: the aggregated digital characterization exists,
is current as of `assertion.reread_commit`, and reports Fmax, area and
power across a declared corner set with the response JSON behind every
figure named.
WHAT IT DOES NOT MEAN: that the digital partition is verified. The
rung-2 gate-level SPICE replay is NOT PASSING (six campaigns, latest
records FAIL or ERROR as of the re-read commit, under active
root-causing), and the routed macro has no LVS and no extracted SPEF.
All three are stated in the section this wraps. T1 item 5 (full corner
verification) and item 4 (LVS clean) are `unmet` on this partition in
the committed report, and those are the rows that grade those
questions.
A NOTE ON THE FUNCTIONAL HALF BEING A POINTER RATHER THAN A
TRANSCRIPTION. The gate-level campaigns mint a new record every day or
two. Transcribing their figures would make the wrapped document stale on
the day it was written -- the exact defect class this whole issue
exists to close -- so the section names the campaigns, their current
disposition and the decision records that settle the accepted findings,
and tells the reader to read each campaign's own latest record. That is
a deliberate scoping choice, recorded here so a future re-asserter does
not read it as an omission.
summary: Digital partition (sar_ctrl_a): sim/characterization-summary.md's 'Digital partition' section aggregates Fmax (163.00-584.03 MHz post-route across 5 corners, vs a 16.00 MHz requirement), area (7968.400 um^2 routed die, exactly the reserved footprint) and estimated power (0.2260-0.3476 mW) across the corner set, per T1 item 8's digital sentence. PASS IS ABOUT THE REPORT, NOT THE PARTITION: the rung-2 gate-level SPICE replay is not passing, and there is no LVS and no SPEF for the routed macro -- all stated in the section, and all graded by items 4 and 5, not item 8.

assertion.scope: sim/characterization-summary.md, section 'Digital partition (sar_ctrl_a) -- Fmax, area and power across the corner set' and its three subsections. The per-spec-row analog table is OUT of this envelope's scope and is asserted by characterization-summary.analog.json.
asserted: Fmax IS reported across a corner set: 331.02 / 163.00 / 230.95 / 415.49 / 584.03 MHz at tt_025C_3v30 / ss_125C_3v00 / ss_n40C_3v00 / ff_125C_3v60 / ff_n40C_3v60, from the five committed post-route klt sta responses. Worst corner 163.00 MHz against DR-0003's 16.00 MHz requirement.

AREA is reported: routed die 7968.400 um^2 (199.210 x 40.000 um), core 7792.96 um^2, utilization 67.72 %, from the committed klt place-and-route response -- and is exactly the ring-exclusive box layout/adc-top/ reserves, which the run's explicit no-margin floorplan makes a fit proof rather than a coincidence.
POWER is reported across the same corner set: 0.2787 / 0.2360 / 0.2260 / 0.3476 / 0.3310 mW, from the same five responses.
Every figure in the section was transcribed from a committed klt response JSON named in the section itself; the section derives nothing.

The section's stated limitations are the ones the underlying records state: no extracted SPEF (LEF/DEF-geometry RC estimate), ideal SDC clock, Fmax extrapolated rather than bisected, interconnect corner nom only, and the 15-corner liberty sweep spanning 1.62-5.50 V deliberately NOT quoted as this block's corner set because most of it lies outside the ratified 2.97-3.63 V supply row.
not_asserted: That the digital partition is functionally verified at rung 2. It is not: six gate-level SPICE-replay campaigns have committed records and each one's latest reads FAIL or ERROR at the re-read commit. The section says so and points at each campaign's own record rather than transcribing figures that move week to week.
That the routed macro has been LVS'd. No golden SPICE reference for the merged GDS is generated in this repo, which is why item 4.digital is uncited in the manifest.
That these timing numbers are SPEF-annotated signoff numbers. They are real routed geometry timed from a LEF/DEF RC estimate.
That the digital power figure may be added to the analog table's Power row. The section explicitly declines to sum them, because nobody has run the combined measurement.

That the whole document has been re-read since `reread_commit`. The rows listed in `assertion.partial_updates` were re-derived and re-cited at a later commit; the rest of the document carries the `reread_commit` vintage.
known_gaps_carried: No klt extract --parasitics SPEF for sar_ctrl_a.
No LVS of the routed sar_ctrl macro (blocks item 4.digital and item 11.digital).
Rung-2 gate-level replay open; accepted findings so far are recorded as DR-0027, DR-0028, DR-0030 and DR-0031.
A seventh campaign directory, sim/sar-logic-timing-gates-bad/, holds a testbench and no record yet.
